transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate your time. Um... I guess I'm here because things have just been really overwhelming lately, and it's completely wearing me down. I hope I don't sound difficult or anything—I really try not to cause trouble—but for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. 

I'm a phlebotomist, so I'm used to looking at bloodwork, and... well, no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I originally saw. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds unreasonable or stubborn to say out loud. I don't want to be a bother, but it's just been so stressful. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you ever experienced times when you believed things that others said weren’t true, or seen or heard things that others couldn’t?

Um... well, no, I definitely don't see or hear things that aren't there. I know how that sounds, and I promise I'm completely grounded in reality. I'm just... well, like I mentioned, it's just this one thing with my dad's lab results. 

I know everyone—my family, the other doctors—they all say I'm wrong and that the numbers are fine. And I really, really hate disagreeing with them, I do. I don't want to be that person who argues with medical professionals, because I respect what you all do so much. But... I saw the original numbers. I know what I saw, and the chart in the system right now just doesn't match. Someone is changing them or holding something back, and I've spent the whole last year just trying to prove it so my dad can get the right care. 

I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds like I'm just being difficult or, I don't know, paranoid. I really don't mean to be. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not coming across as crazy or anything.
Have you ever had any other beliefs that others didn't share or thought were unusual, even if they seemed completely true to you?

Um... no, not really. I mean, nothing else. I really try to be agreeable and see things from other people's perspectives. I know I must sound so fixated on this one thing with my dad's chart, and I'm so sorry if it makes me seem, you know, unreasonable. But honestly, other than this... this situation with the lab results, I don't have any other unusual beliefs or anything like that. I just go to work, do my job, and try to take care of my family. I really hope you don't think I'm just making things up or looking for problems. I'm just trying to do the right thing for my dad. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

Can you tell me more about how you know the lab results were changed? Have you seen any evidence that supports this, or is it something you just feel strongly about despite others not agreeing with you?

Um... well, I really don't want to sound like I'm just being stubborn, and I know how it looks when everyone else is saying the opposite. I completely understand why you'd ask that. But... I drew his blood myself, originally, and I saw the printout before it went into the main system. 

I'm a phlebotomist, so I know what I'm looking at, you know? And when I checked his chart a few days later, the numbers for his kidney function were just... different. They were higher. And some of the secondary markers were just missing entirely. 

I know the other doctors say it's just a clerical thing, or that I misremembered, and I really, really wish I could just agree with them and let it go. It would be so much easier. But I've been trying to prove it for a year now because I know what I saw, and it's just... it's completely wearing me down. I don't want to cause trouble for the clinic, I really don't, but someone is holding back the real results. I'm sorry, I know that sounds like a lot. Am I making any sense at all? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
Have you ever had any beliefs that were completely certain to you, even when others strongly disagreed, outside of this situation with your dad's lab results?

Um... no, definitely not. I mean, I really try to keep an open mind about things, and I always, always try to listen to what other people have to say. I know how important it is to be flexible and not, you know, get stuck in your own head. 

Outside of this one thing with my dad... I don't have any other disagreements with people like that. I really don't. I usually just go along with what makes everyone else comfortable. I hate conflict, honestly. I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just... I really want to make sure you know that I'm not a difficult person, or someone who just argues for the sake of it. I really respect your time and your expertise. 

So, no, nothing else at all. I hope that's... I hope that answers what you were looking for? I just want to be as helpful as I can.
Can you tell me more about how you feel about the clinic staff and whether you believe they are intentionally withholding or changing your father's lab results against his best interest?

Um... well, I really don't want to sound like I'm accusing anyone of being malicious, because I know they're all good people. I really do. I work with them, and I know how hard everyone works. But... yes, I do believe someone is intentionally holding back the real results or changing them. 

I know it sounds terrible to say that out loud, and I'm so sorry if it makes me seem paranoid or something. I really don't want to be that kind of person. But for the past year, I've been trying to prove that this is happening, and it's just... it's exhausting. No matter how many doctors or even my own family members tell me the numbers are fine, I just know the chart doesn't match what I saw. I know it. And it's wearing me down so much. 

I don't think they're doing it to hurt him, exactly, maybe they just made a mistake and are trying to cover it up? Or maybe there's some policy I don't understand? I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt. But the numbers are definitely changed, and they won't admit it. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear, and I really hope you don't think badly of me for saying it. I just... I have to be honest about what I saw, right? Is it okay that I feel this way, even if it's hard for other people to understand?
Has your belief that the lab results were changed ever felt completely certain to you, even when faced with clear evidence that the current chart is accurate?

Um... yes. I know I've brought this up a bit already, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record... I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. I know your time is valuable. But... yes, it does feel completely certain to me. 

Even when they pull up the current chart on the screen and point right at the numbers, and even when my own family members or the other doctors sit me down and tell me everything is perfectly fine... I just... I know the chart doesn't match what I saw. I've spent this whole past year trying to prove it, and no matter what "evidence" they show me from the system, I just can't shake that certainty. 

I really, really wish I could just accept their version of it, because fighting this for a year is just... it's wearing me down so much to be the only one who sees it. I hope I don't sound completely unreasonable when I admit that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest answer I can, even if it makes me look a little stubborn. Does that... does that answer your question okay?

Have you ever had any other experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t agree with, even if they seemed certain you were wrong—outside of this situation with your father’s lab results?

Um... no, definitely not. I think... well, I know you just asked me something similar earlier, and I really hope I'm not misunderstanding you. I want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need. But no, there really hasn't been anything else. 

I've always been the kind of person who just goes with the flow, you know? I really don't like to make waves or be difficult. I've never been one of those people who digs their heels in about things, especially if everyone else is saying I'm wrong. That's why this whole thing with my dad's chart is so... so out of character for me, and so exhausting. 

But aside from this one situation, I promise, I don't have any other beliefs like that. I always listen to what other people tell me. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I really want to be as helpful as possible for you.
